title: Gov Lawal pledges more projects as APC campaign storms Shinkafi LGA
summary: Dauda Lawal pledged further projects in Shinkafi at an APC campaign rally. He highlighted health works and sought support in the 2027 elections.
body:
Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal pledged to deliver more projects in Shinkafi Local Government Area while speaking at the APC Zamfara North campaign flag-off rally on Friday. The event was held at the Eid ground in Shinkafi, where the governor also asked residents to support the party in the 2027 general election.

The rally drew senior party figures, including former governor Abdul’aziz Yari, who is director general of the Tinubu/Shettima Presidential Campaign Council; former governor Mahmuda Aliyu Shinkafi; and Zamfara APC Chairman Kabiru Moyi. Tens of thousands of supporters welcomed the entourage at the city gate, chanting slogans in support of the party.

Lawal thanked Shinkafi residents for their solidarity and reception. He said his administration had made progress in education, healthcare, infrastructure and the economy, and pointed to the referral hospital under construction in Shinkafi as a major project. He described it as a legacy project and said it would mark a turning point for healthcare in Zamfara and the North West.

The governor also said his administration had rehabilitated six primary healthcare centres, including facilities in Badarawa, Birnin Yero, Galadi, Jangeru and Kurya. He reported that 22 of 31 projects had been completed over the previous three and a half years, with the remaining nine ongoing and more than 80 per cent complete. Lawal urged voters to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, himself and the APC in the upcoming election.

title: 2027: Tinubu failed to fulfil his promises, he must go – Obi
summary: Peter Obi urged voters to remove Tinubu in 2027, citing unmet pledges and poverty. He promised power, jobs, unity and security under a government with Rabiu Kwankwaso.
body:
Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, called on voters to remove President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election, saying a change of government was needed for Nigeria to achieve development. Speaking to residents at an event in Aba, Abia State, on Friday, he accused the Tinubu administration of failing to deliver on campaign promises and worsening poverty. Obi also argued that the presidency demanded energy and commitment.

Obi said a government led by him and his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, would work to unite the country and expand economic and social development. He said the proposed administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity, and that borrowing should be directed towards investment. He also pledged to shift the economy from consumption towards production, job creation and prosperity.

The candidate criticised the Federal Government’s borrowing, alleging that the Tinubu administration had borrowed more than previous administrations combined without results visible to Nigerians. He questioned how public loans were being used and said his administration would ensure public funds benefited the public. Obi further claimed that the number of people living in poverty had risen from 87 million when Tinubu took office to more than 140 million. He promised greater investment in education and healthcare, citing youth unemployment as a concern.

On Abia’s economy, Obi pledged to develop Aba into an export hub and connect it with Port Harcourt to create an economic corridor within the first years of his administration. He also promised action on insecurity, including the abduction of schoolchildren, and said national unity would be a priority. Obi described his vision as a country where children from any background could have the opportunity to succeed.

title: Nigeria’s $1bn Monthly Remittance Has Been Achieved – CBN Governor Cardoso
summary: Nigeria has met its $1 billion monthly diaspora-remittance target, the CBN governor said. The bank is aiming for $1.5 billion by mid-2027.
body:
Nigeria has reached its target of $1 billion in monthly diaspora remittances, Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso said at the 61st Annual Bankers’ Dinner of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria in Lagos on Friday. The next goal is to raise monthly inflows to $1.5 billion by the end of the first half of 2027.

Cardoso commended licensed International Money Transfer Operators for strengthening transparency, investing in technology and expanding formal remittance channels, particularly in Asia. He also pointed to greater access to card payments abroad, saying the changes had brought more convenience and helped restore respect for Nigerians overseas.

He said the next phase of financial reforms should deepen liquidity, broaden participation and increase the financial instruments available to businesses and investors. The naira had strengthened by about 6 per cent over the past year, he said, while daily foreign-exchange market turnover had at times exceeded $1 billion. Fixed-income market turnover averaged N1.5 trillion a day, supported by a tradable benchmark yield curve extending to 10 years.

Cardoso described those indicators as signs of growing market confidence, while cautioning that functioning markets do not keep prices static. He said currencies, including the naira, can fluctuate in response to economic fundamentals and global developments, including changes in US interest rates and investor risk sentiment. Nigeria was better equipped to manage external shocks than it had been three years earlier, he said, citing stronger external buffers and the CBN’s readiness to use reserves when necessary to address disorderly market conditions.

title: Oando announces final terms of N203.8 billion rights issue
summary: Oando plans to raise N203.8 billion through a rights issue of about 4.1 billion shares. Eligible shareholders can apply from December 2026.
body:
Oando announces final terms of N203.8 billion rights issue

Oando Plc plans to raise N203.8 billion by offering about 4.1 billion ordinary shares to existing shareholders. The shares, with a nominal value of 50 kobo each, will be offered at N50 apiece on a one-for-two basis. The company said it has secured the regulatory approvals needed to proceed.

In a regulatory filing, Oando linked the capital raise to its acquisition of Nigerian Agip Oil Company from Eni in August 2024, in a transaction valued at $783 million. The acquisition increased Oando’s participating interest in OMLs 60 to 63 from 20 per cent to 40 per cent and transferred operatorship of the assets to the company. Oando said the deal expanded its upstream operations and created opportunities to invest in production growth and cash generation.

The company expects the proceeds to strengthen its balance sheet, improve working capital and support the development of new oil and gas wells across its core upstream assets. Chief Executive Wale Tinubu said Oando’s focus was to turn the expanded asset base into sustained production growth, stronger cash generation and long-term shareholder value. He said a stronger capital structure would help fund operations and investment and provide financial flexibility.

Oando said it has approvals from Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission and Nigerian Exchange, as well as the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and the Financial Surveillance Department of the South African Reserve Bank. Eligible shareholders on the Nigerian register are those listed at the close of business on 13 February 2026; the qualifying date for shareholders on the South African register is 4 December 2026. The acceptance period is scheduled to open on 7 December 2026 and close on 15 January 2027. Shareholders on the South African register will pay R0.632487 per rights share.

title: ‘Not a chance’ – Fulham coach Arbeloa rules out Calvin Bassey sale
summary: Alvaro Arbeloa says Fulham will not sell Calvin Bassey in January amid reported interest from Manchester United. The club is discussing a new contract.
body:
Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has ruled out Calvin Bassey leaving the club during the January transfer window, despite reported interest from Manchester United and other clubs. Arbeloa said the Nigeria international is an important part of his squad and that Fulham have no intention of selling him midway through the season.

Speaking at a press conference before Fulham’s match against Bournemouth, Arbeloa said he was pleased with Bassey and regarded him as one of the team’s captains and leaders. He also said he believed the defender was happy at the club. Arbeloa’s comments dismissed the possibility of Manchester United securing Bassey’s services in January.

The manager highlighted Bassey’s value beyond his defensive performances, pointing to his leadership and role in the team’s defensive setup. He treated reported interest from other clubs as recognition of the player’s performances and growing importance to Fulham, rather than as a reason for concern.

Fulham are understood to be in discussions with Bassey over a new contract, a step that could make a move more difficult for interested clubs. The 26-year-old joined Fulham from Ajax in 2023 and has become an important figure in the squad. He previously played for Rangers and is also a regular member of Nigeria’s national team, featuring prominently for the Super Eagles in international competitions.

title: FG clears pension backlog accumulated since 2013 – PTAD
summary: PTAD says the government has cleared inherited Defined Benefit Scheme liabilities. The minimum monthly pension is now N58,000, up from N6,024 in 2024.
body:
The Federal Government has cleared outstanding unfunded pension liabilities inherited by the Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD) since it began administering the Defined Benefit Scheme (DBS) in 2013, Executive Secretary Tolulope Odunaiya said at a stakeholders’ forum in Lagos. She said the budget line for those liabilities is expected to fall to zero in 2027, as no further funding will be needed to settle them under the scheme.

Odunaiya said the minimum monthly pension paid under the DBS had risen to N58,000 from N6,024 in 2024. She attributed the increase to pension increments and a harmonisation policy, which calculates entitlements using the salary structure applicable at the scheme’s 2007 cut-off date rather than the structure in place when an individual retired. PTAD said eligible pensioners had received all arrears arising from the harmonisation and other increases. Monthly pension disbursements have grown from about N8bn to more than N13bn, Odunaiya added.

The directorate is working with the National Health Insurance Authority on nationwide healthcare coverage for DBS pensioners, with implementation set to be prioritised in 2027. PTAD has also upgraded its verification system and Aliveness Confirmation Portal so pensioners can complete annual checks remotely using electronic devices. Officials demonstrated those tools, an integrated automation system and an online complaints portal at the forum.

Public Complaints Commission Chief Commissioner Bashir Abubakar, represented at the event by Deputy Director of Investigation Amusat Medinat, said PTAD had resolved about 80 per cent of pension-related cases referred by the commission. He said many unresolved cases involved missing documents or failure to follow instructions, and that a dedicated desk officer would coordinate with PTAD’s Lagos office.

The Nigeria Union of Pensioners welcomed the clearance of arrears and the planned health scheme, while urging PTAD to ensure pension increases remain part of regular payments. The union also called for monitoring to ensure security-related palliatives reach their intended recipients. PTAD said it would continue working to maintain regular payments and improve its services.

title: 2027: Tinubu Will Lose If Election Is Free, Fair – Baba-Ahmed
summary: PRP chairman Hakeem Baba-Ahmed says Tinubu is vulnerable in 2027 if the election is fair. He also raised concerns about campaigning, security and electoral conditions.
body:
Peoples Redemption Party National Chairman Hakeem Baba-Ahmed says President Bola Tinubu could lose the 2027 presidential election if it is conducted freely and fairly. In an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, he described Tinubu as beatable and said he believed the president could lose in many states.

Baba-Ahmed argued that dissatisfaction with the administration could weaken Tinubu’s prospects for a second term. He dismissed concerns that opposition parties could not challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress, and said crowds at APC rallies did not necessarily show genuine support. He alleged that some people attending rallies were transported there and paid to take part.

He called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to provide a level playing field and said he hoped the judiciary would act fairly. Baba-Ahmed also raised concerns about electoral violence and whether security agencies could maintain order, warning that these conditions might restrict opposition parties’ ability to campaign. He criticised arrests of people for shouting “Bamayi,” arguing that such expressions should not be treated as offences.

Baba-Ahmed contrasted the coming contest with the 2023 election, saying Tinubu had received substantial support from the North because voters expected him to address serious problems. He claimed the Northwest had since turned away from the president. Tinubu won the 2023 election with 8,794,726 votes, ahead of Atiku Abubakar, who received 6,984,520, and Peter Obi, who received 6,101,533. Opposition candidates challenged the result, but the Presidential Election Petition Tribunal and Supreme Court upheld Tinubu’s victory. The 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, followed by governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6.

title: ‎2027: Delta CP warns officers against partisanship, extortion
summary: Delta police chief Samuel Erale directed senior officers to remain politically neutral ahead of the 2027 elections. He also vowed action against extortion and misconduct.
body:
Delta State Commissioner of Police Samuel Erale has instructed senior officers to remain politically neutral ahead of the 2027 general elections and warned them against colluding with political parties or candidates. He issued the directive at a Thursday conference, following guidance from Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu. Erale said people should receive equal police protection regardless of political affiliation and urged officers to safeguard the public and the electoral process.

He told Area Commanders and Divisional Police Officers to work with campaign organisers on safety arrangements. If a planned venue cannot be policed effectively, he said, organisers should move the event to a more secure location where adequate protection can be provided.

The commissioner also called on officers to build stronger ties with the communities they serve. He urged them to maintain contact with residents and community leaders and use local intelligence to identify emerging security concerns. Amid a rising number of complaints about police conduct, Erale reaffirmed the command’s zero tolerance for extortion and corruption. He directed senior officers to improve supervision, respond promptly to complaints and hold personnel accountable, while mentoring junior officers.

The instructions come amid reports of violence connected to political campaigning in Delta. Six people were reported killed and several others injured at a campaign event in Uduere, in Ughelli North. A day earlier, the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate Ovie Omo-Agege alleged that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour, killing four people and critically injuring four others. The police confirmed that the state government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North, from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. daily, until further notice. The Nigeria Democratic Congress, the Nigerian Bar Association and the Pan Niger Delta Forum have called for an investigation.

title: 16 Killed As Gunmen Attack Plateau Community
summary: At least 16 people were reported killed in an attack on Tafi Gana in Plateau State. Police put the toll at 17; four others were injured.
body:
An attack on Tafi Gana, a hamlet in Kyie Ihwien near Jebbu Miango in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, left at least 16 people dead and four injured, according to the Irigwe Development Association (IDA). The police gave a higher death toll of 17, with the same number of people injured. The victims included children and elderly residents.

The IDA said armed attackers carrying assault rifles and other weapons invaded the community on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. Its account placed the attack at about 11:30 p.m. and said around 16 people were found dead by daybreak the following morning. The police statement, by contrast, said preliminary investigations put the time at about 11:55 a.m. on November 25.

The Plateau State Police Command said officers were sent to the scene after receiving a report. The assailants fled into nearby bushes when they saw the approaching police team, according to police spokesperson SP Alfred Alabo. The command said the injured were taken to hospital and the bodies of those killed were placed in a hospital morgue pending further investigation.

The area’s traditional ruler, Nggwe Gado Dama, said the incident had been reported to the Divisional Police Headquarters in Bassa and the commander of Sector 3 of Operation Enduring Peace. He said security personnel were at the scene. The IDA condemned the killings, urged residents not to take the law into their own hands and called on them to let security agencies investigate and pursue those responsible. It also offered condolences to the bereaved families and the Rigwe community. Police Commissioner Sunday Okoebor said the command was committed to residents’ safety and had put measures in place to prevent a recurrence.

title: Africa begins rollout of cheaper HIV prevention injection
summary: Lower-cost generic lenacapavir has arrived in Zambia, with Uganda next. The twice-yearly HIV prevention injection is expected to cost about $40 per person annually.
body:
Supplies of a lower-cost generic version of lenacapavir, a long-acting HIV prevention medicine, have begun arriving in Africa. The first global shipment reached Zambia, and Uganda is expected to receive supplies in the coming days, according to the Global Fund. Zimbabwe is due to receive supplies early next year, with other African countries scheduled to follow.

The injection is administered twice a year and is expected to cost about $40 per person annually. That is substantially less than the original version developed by Gilead Sciences, which reportedly cost about $28,000 a year in the United States. Lenacapavir targets HIV’s protective protein shell, disrupting the virus’s ability to multiply and establish infection.

In 2024 clinical trials involving more than 5,000 adolescent girls and young women in Uganda and South Africa, none of the participants who received the injection contracted HIV. The World Health Organization recommended lenacapavir for HIV prevention in July 2025. Unlike pre-exposure prophylaxis, or PrEP, which generally involves taking medication daily, the injection may offer an alternative for people who find daily pills difficult or face stigma associated with using them.

The Global Fund says more than 189,000 people in 10 countries have already received their first lenacapavir injections. It expects 24 countries to receive supplies by the end of 2026 and, with support from the United States government, aims to reach at least three million people by the end of 2028. The medicine is eventually expected to be available in 120 low- and middle-income countries.

Sub-Saharan Africa accounts for nearly two-thirds of people living with HIV worldwide, and adolescent girls and young women are disproportionately affected. The rollout comes amid concerns that cuts to US foreign assistance could affect HIV programmes in countries reliant on international funding. The United Nations has set a goal of ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.

title: NANS hails FG’s move to manufacture passports
summary: NANS welcomed plans for a National Passport Manufacturing Centre, calling domestic production a step toward sovereignty. It also praised passport-system reforms.
body:
The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has welcomed the establishment of a National Passport Manufacturing Centre, describing the move as a step towards reducing foreign dependence and strengthening Nigeria’s sovereignty. The association also praised Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo for leading the initiative and for reforms to the passport system.

NANS President Akinteye Babatunde Afeez made the remarks in a statement issued on Thursday. He called the centre a historic achievement, saying Nigeria had not produced its own international passports in the more than six decades since independence. The association described the centre’s groundbreaking ceremony as a significant milestone for national identity and public service delivery.

The students’ body said reforms to passport applications and renewals had eased delays and bureaucratic difficulties faced by Nigerians. It said the changes had benefited students studying abroad and other Nigerians living outside the country by making it easier to obtain or renew travel documents. These assessments were made by the association in its statement.

NANS also praised Tunji-Ojo’s leadership at the Ministry of Interior, saying it had broadened perceptions of the ministry’s work. The association credited him with changing the status quo in passport services and commended President Bola Tinubu for appointing him to the role.

The association said it would continue to recognise policies and initiatives that improve people’s lives, expand opportunities and strengthen Nigeria’s sovereignty. It described the passport manufacturing centre as the latest in a series of reforms introduced under the minister.

title: 2027: Violence, Intimidation, Use Of Thugs May Discourage Voters, Amupitan Warns Political Parties
summary: INEC Chair Joash Amupitan warned parties that campaign violence and intimidation could deter voters and erode confidence. He urged issue-based campaigning and lawful conduct.
body:
Independent National Electoral Commission Chairman Joash Amupitan has condemned violence linked to political campaigns, warning parties and their supporters that intimidation and the use of thugs could undermine the 2027 general election. He spoke on Thursday at a meeting between the commission and security agencies focused on strengthening election security ahead of the poll.

Amupitan urged political actors to campaign on issues, respect opposing views and stay within the law. He said political ambition should not come at the cost of citizens’ lives. Violence and intimidation recently reported during campaigns in some states, he warned, could discourage people from voting and weaken public confidence in the democratic process.

The INEC chairman said the commission was working with the Office of the National Security Adviser, led by Nuhu Ribadu, to identify potential flash points across the country. He described election security as a shared responsibility, requiring relevant agencies to work together to address violence, intimidation and other threats to credible elections.

Amupitan also called on security agencies to act professionally and impartially and to respect the rule of law. He warned that political interests must not interfere with their constitutional duties. Inspector-General of Police Tunji Disu, State Security Service Director-General Oluwatosin Ajayi and other officials attended the meeting.

In his welcoming address, Disu stressed the importance of stronger collaboration, intelligence sharing and coordinated security operations to respond to potential threats to the electoral process.

title: Bukarti and DanBello: When is it haram to support a politician in Nigeria?, By Yushau A. Shuaib
summary: A commentary argues that supporting a candidate or providing lawful campaign services is not inherently forbidden. It condemns intimidation and urges clearer disclosure of political ties.
body:
A commentary by Yushau A. Shuaib argues that Nigerians should be free to support candidates, join political parties or provide professional services to lawful campaigns without facing intimidation. It contends that political violence and efforts to damage people’s reputations—not political participation itself—are the greater threat to civic engagement.

The essay focuses on Bulama Bukarti and DanBello, two public figures whose possible involvement in politics has prompted criticism. Neither, Shuaib writes, had publicly responded to the allegations at the time of his article. He suggests that their failure to explain their positions before speculation grew left room for claims of betrayal. Shuaib says he understands Bukarti to be supporting a candidate he considers capable, and DanBello to be providing strategic communications and advocacy consultancy.

As a comparison, Shuaib points to Islamic scholar and public intellectual Ali Isa Pantami, who entered politics and joined a party he had previously criticised while in government. The essay says Pantami faced attacks from some fellow critics but defended his decision with reasoned arguments. Shuaib also argues that public and private political behaviour can differ, and that such differences do not by themselves establish dishonesty.

Shuaib condemns reports of the alleged stoning of President Tinubu’s convoy and attacks on praise-singer Kahutu Rarara, including in places of worship. He also discloses that he advised on a campaign opposing the Tinubu Must Go movement after being approached by Malam Kashifu Inuwa. He says he recommended the name Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation and urged factual messaging focused on peacebuilding and good governance; he says those recommendations were implemented with the tacit support of First Lady Oluremi Tinubu.

The author says he is making that disclosure to demonstrate the value of transparency in political engagement. His central argument is that opposition and support are both legitimate parts of democratic participation, while violence and coercion are unacceptable regardless of who uses them.

title: Alia sets up panel to review 2023 manifesto
summary: Benue Governor Hyacinth Alia named a 17-member panel to review his 2023 manifesto ahead of the 2027 election. It will assess progress, gaps and priorities.
body:
Benue State Governor Hyacinth Alia has appointed a 17-member committee to review the manifesto he campaigned on in 2023 and prepare a revised document ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The committee’s formation was announced in a statement issued on Wednesday by Tersoo Kula, the governor’s chief press secretary and communications director for the Tinubu/Alia Campaign Council in Benue State.

The members are Prof. Gabriel Akpen, Prof. Jerome Andohol, Nick Agule, Peter Sani Ochijele, Vincent Gisaor, Iorwuese Viashima, Sam Yuwa, Tersoo Kula, Sylvester Onmoke, Bishop Reuben Angula, Gabriel Uketor Moti, George Genyi, Tersoo Akula, Elizabeth Shuluwa, Bernard Hom, Elijah Ikpanor and Nick Eworo.

Alia said the committee would examine how much of the original manifesto had been implemented and identify achievements, unfinished work and new challenges facing residents. He urged members to consider what should continue, what needs adjustment and which issues should receive greater priority. He also said recommendations should reflect people’s experiences and the state’s changing economic and social conditions.

The governor said the revised manifesto should link the work already undertaken by his administration with its proposed agenda for a second term. He called for goals that are practical, measurable and responsive to communities across Benue. Alia asked the committee to work transparently and promptly, and to deliver an actionable plan. He said he would support its work and expected the final document to help sustain the administration’s efforts and improve governance.

title: 2027: FCT, Rivers in the bag, give me Imo and Kwara, Wike begs Tinubu
summary: Nyesom Wike asked Tinubu to assign him Imo and Kwara for 2027 re-election campaigning, saying preparations in Rivers and the FCT were complete. He cited divisions in the two states.
body:
FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has asked President Bola Tinubu and the director general of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Abubakar Yari, to assign him Imo and Kwara states to mobilise support for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. Speaking at a Rainbow Coalition town hall in Gokana, Rivers State, on Wednesday, Wike said political preparations in Rivers and the Federal Capital Territory were already in place.

“I am done with these states,” Wike said, referring to Rivers and the FCT, which he said he had been assigned to coordinate. He said he wanted to work in Imo because he had heard of political problems there. For Kwara, he said his understanding of divisions in the state came from social media and had not been confirmed.

Wike also urged Gokana residents to support a second term for Tinubu. He praised the president’s decisions on removing the fuel subsidy and increasing allocations to state and local governments, and cited the establishment of the Federal University of Environment in Ogoniland. He encouraged residents to maintain their political relationship with Tinubu rather than move towards an uncertain alternative.

The minister praised local stakeholders for working together through the Rainbow Coalition, a campaign group that has drawn him into disputes with Imo Governor Hope Uzodimma and Kwara Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq. Coalition coordinator in Gokana Kenneth Kobani said the meeting brought together different parts of the community. APC South-South National Vice Chairman Victor Tombari Giadom predicted the coalition could secure up to 90 per cent of Gokana’s votes in 2027, while Senator Magnus Abe credited Wike with helping reconcile divided political leaders.

title: Senate Decries Inadequate LPG Supply, Considers Price Reduction
summary: The Senate gas committee says weak domestic LPG supply threatens efforts to lower cooking-gas costs. It will continue talks with industry stakeholders on supply and remittances.
body:
The Senate Committee on Gas Resources has raised concerns that insufficient supplies of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to the domestic market could frustrate efforts to reduce cooking-gas costs for Nigerians. Committee chairman Senator Jarigbe Jarigbe made the remarks during a meeting with gas-sector stakeholders focused on export revenue remittances and local supply.

Jarigbe said the supply situation ran counter to the aims of Presidential Executive Order 9, issued by President Bola Tinubu on February 13, 2026. He said the order was intended to support adequate domestic LPG availability, improve revenue remittances and bring down gas prices. The senator stressed that more product must reach the local market to ease the financial pressure on households.

The committee plans to continue discussions with industry participants, including Chevron, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited. Jarigbe said the engagement would focus on securing adequate domestic supply and achieving the intended reduction in prices.

Enorense Amadasu, representing the regulatory commission, said the offshore facility was initially designed around export evacuation arrangements for both the Nigerian side and Chevron under their joint venture. He cited infrastructure and logistical limitations as obstacles to moving offshore LPG into the domestic market. The committee is expected to meet relevant stakeholders again next Tuesday to address supply gaps, improve export revenue remittances and increase LPG availability in Nigeria.

title: Father, son jailed for smuggling £500,000 cannabis into UK
summary: A father and son were jailed after bringing 50.25kg of cannabis from Bangkok to Heathrow. The NCA says airport drug-courier arrests have risen sharply.
body:
A father and his 20-year-old son have been jailed for importing cannabis worth about £500,000 into the United Kingdom from Thailand. Alec Peter Chadwick, 39, and Riley Peter Emerson-Chadwick were arrested by Border Force officers at Heathrow Airport in July after arriving from Bangkok, the National Crime Agency (NCA) said.

Officers found a combined 50.25kg of cannabis in their luggage. Emerson-Chadwick had 33.5kg in his suitcase and Chadwick had 16.75kg. Both pleaded guilty to importing Class B drugs at Wimbledon Magistrates’ Court later that day.

At Isleworth Crown Court, Chadwick was sentenced to two years and eight months in prison, while his son received a two-year jail term. The NCA said organised crime groups often use social media to recruit couriers, offering free holidays and spending money in return for carrying drugs.

The agency reported that 142 cannabis smugglers were arrested at UK airports in 2023, followed by 801 in 2024 and 976 in 2025. It said 600 air-passenger drug couriers had been arrested at UK airports during the first six months of 2026, putting the year on course to exceed the previous total.

NCA senior investigating officer Peter Jones warned people against accepting offers from criminal networks, saying there was no such thing as a free holiday. He said couriers risked prison, criminal convictions and harm to their future career and travel prospects. Jones also warned that proceeds from cannabis smuggling can fund the trafficking of other drugs and contribute to wider criminal activity.

title: 2027: No margin for error, INEC warns RECs, sets 6 operational priorities
summary: INEC chair Joash Amupitan warned state commissioners that 2027 polls leave no room for error. He set six priorities covering technology, logistics, security and neutrality.
body:
Independent National Electoral Commission Chairman Joash Amupitan has warned Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) that the 2027 general elections leave no margin for operational error. At a strategic meeting in Abuja, he set six priorities and called for prompt, documented action and personal accountability from the officials responsible for state-level preparations.

Amupitan said reviews of recent off-cycle polls—including governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun, FCT Area Council elections and 16 legislative bye-elections—showed the value of early planning, orderly logistics and close supervision. He said problems identified in those exercises must be addressed before a nationwide simulation and ahead of the general elections. Presidential and National Assembly polls are scheduled for January 16, 2027, followed by governorship and State House of Assembly elections on February 6. INEC’s plans cover more than 100 million registered voters and 177,299 polling units, including provisions for 232,658 voters with disabilities.

The first priority is a mock accreditation and result-transmission exercise on November 28, 2026, in two polling units per ward. RECs are to oversee preparations and send INEC headquarters a technical report by November 30 covering network gaps, device faults and procedural obstacles. The second is last-mile logistics, including checks on transport arrangements and the readiness and security of Registration Area Centres. Third is enforcing a limit of 850 registered voters per Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) device, down from 1,250. Amupitan said INEC had acquired 57,000 additional devices and directed commissioners to ensure equipment is charged, configured, accounted for and backed up in high-density areas.

The fourth priority is extending the ICCES security framework to every local government area and ward, working with police, security officials and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. Election risk maps are to help identify potential flashpoints and resolve disputes over campaign rally locations or timing in advance. Fifth is recruiting, training and supporting more than 1.41 million temporary election workers, including National Youth Service Corps members, academics and civil servants. Amupitan stressed that their safety, competence and timely allowances matter to effective field operations.

The sixth priority is preventing information gaps, disinformation and partisan conduct. Amupitan urged regular engagement with political parties, observers, civil society groups and the media, and said staff who breach electoral rules or compromise neutrality would not be shielded. He also told RECs to supervise field audits themselves, report conditions candidly and stay in close contact with electoral officers so headquarters can respond to problems quickly.

title: What separates consistent traders from everyone else?
summary: Consistent trading is less about winning every position than applying a defined process. Preparation, risk limits and review help traders manage uncertainty and emotion.
body:
Consistency in trading does not mean winning every position or predicting every market move. It means following a defined approach and making decisions that can be reviewed and improved. Prices respond to factors such as economic data, central-bank expectations, geopolitical events, liquidity and investor sentiment—forces traders cannot control. Preparation and discipline are among the factors they can control.

Before entering a trade, experienced traders assess the broader market setting, including trends, relevant price levels, upcoming news, liquidity zones and points that would invalidate the idea. They consider the setup, the potential risks and whether the opportunity justifies taking those risks, rather than reacting solely to rapid price changes.

A plan also sets out entry and exit points, stop losses and risk levels in advance. This does not remove emotions: fear can prompt an early sale, greed can encourage a trader to stay in too long, and frustration can lead to revenge trading. Overconfidence after a run of wins may also result in oversized positions. Rules can help keep these reactions from driving decisions, particularly during volatile periods.

Consistent traders treat trading as a series of decisions, not a judgment based on one position or day. They focus on the quality of their process, risk management and learning from past trades instead of chasing each market move. Education, market knowledge and tools to analyse conditions, track instruments and manage accounts can support more informed decisions. The central distinction is structure, not certainty: traders prepare, manage risk and review their actions. Trading Forex and CFDs involves significant risk and can result in the loss of invested capital. This article is for informational purposes and is not investment advice.

title: Senegal Deny Contact With CAS In 2025 AFCON Row
summary: Senegal’s Fall denied allegations of contact with a CAS arbitrator before the panel awarded Senegal the AFCON title. Morocco may appeal on procedural grounds.
body:
A Senegalese figure named Fall has denied allegations that he contacted a member of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) before its panel ruled in Senegal’s favour in the dispute over the Africa Cup of Nations final. The Moroccan federation (FRMF) had claimed that contact took place between Fall and German arbitrator Ulrich Haas 48 hours before the three-member panel unanimously awarded the trophy to Senegal.

“That is absolutely false. I have never had any exchange with any member of CAS,” Fall said on Senegalese private television channel TFM. He said he was surprised by the accusation and had not contacted anyone in connection with the case.

Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time in January. The Confederation of African Football (CAF) later overturned the result and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory and the title. The decision followed a protest by Senegal’s players after a penalty was awarded to the hosts while the match was goalless. Many Senegalese players left the pitch, but they later returned and the final continued.

CAF’s Appeals Committee had relied on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those provisions say a team that refuses to play or leaves the ground before the match ends without the referee’s authorisation is considered to have lost and is eliminated from the competition. The CAS panel concluded that the referee’s decision to restart the match showed the conditions for resuming play had been met, so the articles did not apply in this case.

The FRMF can appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court. That court does not reconsider the merits of the dispute, but may intervene on procedural matters.

title: NRS seeks simpler tax rules for creative sector
summary: Nigeria’s Revenue Service is urging clearer, simpler tax rules for creative businesses. It says effective tax administration should support investment and growth.
body:
The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and more business-friendly tax rules to encourage investment in the country’s creative economy. The appeal was made at a high-level dialogue on taxation and investment during the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) event in Lagos. The Service said digital business models, intellectual-property-based enterprises and cross-border transactions require rules that creators, entrepreneurs and investors can understand and navigate.

NRS Executive Chairman Dr. Zacch Adedeji, represented at the dialogue by Executive Director for People, Stakeholders and Communication Obinna Ihedioha, described the creative economy as an important source of employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment and economic opportunity. He said it had grown beyond entertainment as digital platforms changed how creative work is produced and commercialised. Businesses, he noted, increasingly build on copyrights, designs, brands and digital products.

Adedeji said tax administration needs to adapt to these developments without discouraging innovation or business expansion. While government requires sustainable revenue for areas including education, security, technology and infrastructure, he said the design of tax rules can influence whether businesses start, attract investment and grow, or remain small.

He said new tax laws present an opportunity to make the system more efficient through clearer regulations, lower compliance burdens for small businesses and better support for taxpayers. The Service also emphasised that formalising a creative business should offer practical benefits, such as access to finance, contracts, investment, wider markets and legal protection.

NRS activities at CANEX included the high-level dialogue and an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors. The Service also presented the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative (CETII), which it said is intended to maintain engagement beyond the event.

title: Disability groups, others demand representation, funding ahead of 2027 polls
summary: Disability advocates urged parties and 2027 candidates to commit to meaningful representation. They also called for funding and stronger enforcement of Nigeria’s disability law.
body:
Disability groups call for representation and funding ahead of 2027 polls

The Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPWD) has urged political parties and candidates seeking office in 2027 to engage people with disabilities and commit to their representation in governance. Speaking at the third Conference of Stakeholders on Disability Inclusion in Nigeria, JONAPWD President Abdullahi Usman said people with disabilities should have a role in leadership and decisions affecting their lives, not be included only as voters.

Usman said the disability community could use its collective political influence to press candidates for specific commitments. He criticised parties for treating people with disabilities as symbolic participants rather than giving them meaningful decision-making roles. He also called on federal and state governments to adequately fund the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities and similar state bodies, saying commissions cannot implement the law without resources.

Nigeria’s Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act was enacted in 2018 and signed into law in January 2019, establishing the national commission. At the conference, MacArthur Foundation Deputy Director Amina Salihu said legislation alone would not improve people’s daily lives without accountability and measurable implementation. She pointed to the Act’s requirement that people with disabilities make up at least five per cent of public-organisation workforces, and cited barriers such as inaccessible public buildings and the lack of sign-language interpreters in recruitment. She also urged disability organisations to ensure women, young people and other marginalised members have influence in their own decision-making.

Nigeria Civil Society Situation Room convener Yunusa Ya’u said commissions need sustained advocacy and implementation, and urged disability groups to develop an inclusion agenda for engagement with candidates. Omar Alihashi of the Canadian High Commission said political inclusion should extend from voting to contesting elections, shaping policy and holding office. ECOWAS Commission programme officer Abimbola Oyelohunnu called for investment in technology, disability data, training and early identification of children with disabilities, as well as recognition of care costs in social protection policies.

title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
summary: Police say six people died in violence at a Delta campaign event; a curfew is in force as an investigation continues. A court also voided Omo-Agege’s nomination.
body:
Political Signals: The Price Of Participation

Police said six people died in violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North, Delta State, on Monday. The preliminary figure, announced Tuesday, is higher than the four deaths first reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. Authorities have imposed a daily curfew across Ughelli North from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. The NDC has alleged official complicity, while the Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised accountability. Those claims remain distinct from the findings of the investigation.

The Federal High Court in Warri on Tuesday nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove his name. Reports attributed the ruling to failures involving the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were not available in initial reports. The judgment and the campaign violence are separate matters; their timing does not establish a connection. Any appeal, interim order or subsequent INEC action could affect the candidacy’s status.

In Lagos, President Bola Tinubu met with Igbo stakeholders, who the presidency said pledged support. Tinubu offered assurances of inclusive governance, while traders’ representative Tony Nwakeze requested loans at five per cent interest to help businesses expand and move towards manufacturing. No operational loan scheme was announced. The Central Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee retained the benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent, underscoring the tension between economic stability and demands for more affordable business financing.

Opposition parties are due to hold a summit on November 30, after postponing it from November 23. Organisers say participating parties and candidates are expected to endorse a framework for cooperation, democratic renewal and reform; no common presidential candidate has been announced. INEC has also selected 17,676 polling units for a nationwide mock accreditation and results-upload exercise on November 28, scheduled to run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The test will allow participants to assess the technology, while published findings and documented follow-up would help the public judge how problems are addressed. The Delta killings make campaign safety an immediate concern alongside candidate eligibility and election readiness.

title: NANS threatens to shut down university over SUG president’s arrest
summary: NANS says it will mobilise students to shut UNIOSUN and occupy the Osun secretariat over the SUG president’s arrest. The university cites an alleged assault.
body:
The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has threatened to mobilise students to shut down Osun State University (UNIOSUN) and occupy the Osun State Government Secretariat over the arrest and prosecution of the university’s Students’ Union Government president. NANS National President Akinteye Afeez announced the proposed action in a statement, alleging that Vice-Chancellor Clement Adebooye ordered the student leader’s arrest.

Afeez said NANS had instructed its zonal coordinator and the Osun State Joint Campus Committee chairman to organise the shutdown and a peaceful occupation of the secretariat. He called for Adebooye’s immediate removal and said the association’s national structures had been activated to relocate to Osun State until the matter was resolved. The statement did not give a date for the planned action or specify the alleged offence for which the student leader was charged.

The university has offered a different account. It said SUG activities had been suspended following an alleged assault on first-year student Emmanuel Onifade by union executives. The university identified the officials as SUG president Layonu Akintayo, assistant general secretary Adesanmi Tijesunimi and faculty chairman Oyedeji Samsideen. It alleged that Onifade had used the university’s logo and the Office of Student Affairs as the identity of a WhatsApp platform, and had threatened another student over a social media video concerning UNIOSUN students.

According to the university, the SUG president asked Onifade to meet at the main campus after the other student raised the matter with union executives. The university alleged that Onifade was then taken in a Students’ Union vehicle to a mechanic workshop in Osogbo, where he was beaten, and was assaulted again at another location. He was reportedly released with serious injuries, after which his father reported the matter to police. The university said the three executives were handed over to police and charged before a magistrate’s court in Oke-Fia. They were granted administrative bail, and the case was adjourned until 23 December. The suspension of SUG activities will remain in place while investigations continue, the university said.

title: Omo-Agege attack: Makinde campaign accuses APC of political violence
summary: A Makinde campaign organisation accused the APC of political violence after an attack in Delta State killed six people. It urged an end to intimidation ahead of the 2027 elections.
body:
The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of promoting political violence following an attack in Delta State that killed six people. The incident involved members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege. The organisation said the attack took place on November 23 and warned that violence could threaten peaceful competition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a statement issued by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO alleged that APC agents were responsible. It said the incident raised concern about a possible wider effort to use armed groups against opposition parties and disrupt peaceful elections. These claims were presented by the campaign organisation; the supplied material contains no response from the APC.

The group cited remarks President Bola Tinubu made to supporters before the 2023 elections, saying they could encourage political confrontation. It also referred to an alleged threat by Edo State APC Chairman Jarret Tenebe to use AK-47 power against those opposing the party’s plan to secure Tinubu’s re-election. The MDPCO criticised the APC leadership for what it described as a failure to condemn the alleged threat or take decisive action against members accused of violence.

The organisation further alleged that opposition parties had faced attacks in Sokoto, Kebbi, Edo, Lagos, Cross River, Kaduna and Kano states, and described the Delta incident as part of a troubling pattern. It called for an immediate end to attempts to suppress political participation and said parties should respect voters’ freedom to choose their leaders. The group also urged Nigerians to support its principal, Seyi Makinde, whom it identified as the Allied Peoples Movement’s presidential candidate, and said his proposed government would focus on transparency, security and citizens’ welfare.

title: NNPC Dismisses Missing $2.04bn Duke Oil Crude Proceeds Reports
summary: NNPC says $2.04bn in crude proceeds was reconciled against fuel supplies and other payments. It says all 59 cargoes under review were accounted for.
body:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited has rejected reports that $2.04 billion in proceeds from crude cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., is missing or unaccounted for. The company said the amount represents the gross value of 29 cargoes whose proceeds were reconciled under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme.

In a statement issued Tuesday in Abuja, NNPC Chief Corporate Communications Officer Andy Odeh said crude revenues were offset against the cost of refined petroleum products supplied to the Nigerian market. The company said the apparent gap arose because some cargoes did not generate separate dollar receipts. Crude was priced in dollars, while products supplied under the arrangement were sold in naira.

NNPC said all 59 cargoes under review were accounted for and reconciled with their respective beneficiaries. It reported that 30 cargoes were paid for in dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at about $1.96 billion, were remitted in naira to the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services accounts. The remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at about $75.9 million, was paid into the then-designated dollar account of the Federal Inland Revenue Service.

The company said the transactions were reflected in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities. It also defended Duke Oil’s status as a separate trading subsidiary, saying it was incorporated in 1989 as a wholly owned NNPC company. NNPC said the ownership is documented in its corporate history, audited accounts and the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative’s 2023 industry report.

NNPC added that dedicated trading subsidiaries are used in the global oil and gas industry and that transactions between related entities are disclosed under International Financial Reporting Standards.

title: PHOTOS: Dele Alake’s daughter weds in Lagos
summary: Wuraola Alake and Wasem Yaji married in a traditional ceremony at Lagos’s Eko Convention Centre on Sunday. Governors and other public figures attended.
body:
Wuraola Alake, daughter of Minister of Solid Minerals Development Dele Alake, married Wasem Yaji at a traditional wedding ceremony in Lagos on Sunday. The event was held at the Eko Convention Centre and drew family members, political leaders and other prominent guests.

Photographs showed the couple wearing traditional outfits and posing together and with attendees. Dele Alake was also seen greeting guests. Among those present were Femi Gbajabiamila, Chief of Staff to the President; Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and his deputy, Obafemi Hamzat; and Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun.

Other state governors at the ceremony included Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo, Biodun Oyebanji of Ekiti, Babagana Zulum of Borno, Uba Sani of Kaduna and Hope Uzodimma of Imo. Attendees also included Deputy President of the Senate Barau Jibrin, former Ogun State Governor Gbenga Daniel and former Ekiti State Governor Niyi Adebayo. Wasem Yaji is the son of the late Nigerian engineer Aloysius Ahile Yaji.

title: Waste crisis: LAWMA launches nighttime evacuation gangs
summary: LAWMA has begun nighttime waste clearance on the Isheri–Igando–LASU–Iba corridor, with further routes planned. It also plans more than 10 regional offices.
body:
The Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) has launched nighttime waste clearance across the state to address mounting refuse heaps and improve sanitation ahead of the Christmas and New Year festivities. The operation began on Monday night along the Isheri–Igando–LASU–Iba corridor, where teams and heavy-duty equipment were deployed to clear identified waste black spots.

LAWMA Acting Managing Director Olajuwon Akinyemi led the operation at Igando Bus Stop, accompanied by the authority’s acting operations director, Olorunwa Tijani, and finance director, Kunle Adebiyi. Akinyemi said the work would extend to other major routes and busy corridors, including Ojota–Ikorodu Road, the Mushin–Moshalashi axis and the Lekki–Ajah corridor.

The authority said the clean-up is intended to restore Lagos’s environmental appeal and provide a cleaner, healthier setting for residents and visitors during the busy holiday period. To reduce the risk of cleared sites becoming dumping locations again, LAWMA said it was working with traditional institutions on community monitoring and enforcement.

Akinyemi also announced plans to establish more than 10 regional offices across Lagos, describing the restructuring as necessary to decentralise the authority’s operations. He said the offices would bring services closer to communities, improve coordination and accountability, and enable faster responses to sanitation problems.

He appealed for residents’ patience as the state addresses waste-management challenges and urged them to report service failures by Private Sector Participation waste operators through LAWMA’s official communication channels, so the authority can enforce compliance.

title: Police ‌‌‍‌‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠‍‌‌‍‍‌detain man for alleged unlawful possession of firearm
summary: Police in Enugu say Odo Ejiofor, 28, is in custody over alleged unlawful firearm possession. Raids across the state yielded firearms; investigations continue.
body:
Police in Enugu State say Odo Ejiofor, 28, is in custody over the alleged unlawful possession of a firearm. In a statement issued in Enugu on Monday, police spokesperson Daniel Ndukwe said operatives recovered firearms during operations at suspected criminal hideouts across the state on 21 November. The statement gave details of three operations and said investigations were continuing.

At about 7 a.m., the Violent Crime Response Unit’s Anti-Cultism Section raided a suspected hideout at Old Artisan, Enugu, after receiving information. Police said suspects fled and abandoned a pump-action gun, which officers recovered. At about 3:30 p.m., Udenu Area Command operatives raided a suspected hideout at Ugbelle-Ohullor, Obollo Afor, in Udenu Local Government Area. They arrested Ejiofor and recovered a locally made pistol, according to the statement.

At about 6:05 p.m., members of the Violent Crime Response Unit raided a hideout at Abakpa-Nike, Enugu, acting on intelligence, and recovered a pistol. The suspects fled when officers arrived. Police said the location was reportedly used for the sale and consumption of illicit drugs and other criminal activities.

Ndukwe said police were working to identify and arrest the suspects who escaped. Ejiofor is expected to be arraigned after investigations are concluded. Commissioner of Police Fidelis Ogarabe reiterated the command’s commitment to intelligence gathering and targeted operations, and urged residents to provide credible, timely information, which he said would be treated confidentially.

title: ‘This Is A Winning Campaign’, NDC Denies Rift With Obi Over Funding
summary: NDC says Peter Obi has not raised concerns about campaign funding and denies a rift ahead of the 2027 election. The party says it remains focused on the campaign.
body:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council has denied reports of a disagreement with its candidate, Peter Obi, over campaign funding. In a statement issued on Monday, council spokesperson Constance Ikokwu said the claims were false and that the party and candidate remained united ahead of the 2027 general election.

Ikokwu said Obi had neither complained that campaign funds were inadequate nor expressed dissatisfaction with the party’s management of campaign finances. She described reports of a rift as an effort to divide the opposition camp and said the campaign was focused on winning the election.

The spokesperson pointed to Obi’s nationwide engagements as evidence of his commitment to the campaign. She said his activity showed energy and consistency, and characterised the campaign so far as a success. The council also said the party and its candidate shared the objective of winning the 2027 presidential election and offering Nigerians what it called a credible alternative.

The statement urged Nigerians to dismiss what Ikokwu described as manufactured controversies, adding that the party and candidate were united and determined. The clarification follows concerns about the control and management of campaign donations after activist Aisha Yesufu launched a fundraising initiative for Obi’s presidential bid. The statement did not provide further details about the initiative or the campaign’s finances.

title: Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return as backlash grows
summary: Trump backed Nvidia’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO. Lawmakers across parties sought investigations, citing national-security and chip-export concerns.
body:
US President Donald Trump endorsed Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, saying the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national-security risk. Huang, the chipmaker’s co-founder, had resigned less than two weeks earlier amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

Trump said on Truth Social that Nvidia’s board had made the “correct and proper decision.” In a CNBC interview, he said the controversy could even benefit the company by drawing attention to its technology. Trump also said the attorney general had confirmed authorities had no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct, while urging Nvidia to continue examining whether its sales complied with restrictions on advanced chip exports to China.

Democratic leaders Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries called for broad investigations into Nvidia, Trump and senior administration officials. Jeffries singled out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and said national security must not be sacrificed for personal financial gain. House Intelligence Committee Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi said it remained unclear what information Chinese intelligence might have obtained and called for a public congressional hearing. Senator Elizabeth Warren also questioned what role administration officials played in the board’s decision.

Republicans raised concerns as well. Senator John Curtis asked what had changed, noting that the board reversed its position while an independent investigation was unfinished. Senator John Cornyn challenged Trump’s assurance that Huang’s return posed no security risk, while Senator Pete Ricketts said the reinstatement did not remove the need for Huang to testify. Former House speaker Newt Gingrich and outgoing representative Don Bacon also called for scrutiny of the national-security implications.

Huang is scheduled to face closed-door questioning by three House committees on December 1 about his relationship with the woman and Nvidia’s chip exports. The Senate Banking Committee has said his December 3 appearance will be livestreamed. Trump declined to comment on a report that the woman had been in contact with an official from China’s principal intelligence agency.

title: 2027: Ebonyi PDP inaugurates campaign council
summary: Ebonyi PDP has inaugurated a campaign council for the 2027 general elections. It will coordinate statewide campaigning and voter engagement.
body:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State has inaugurated a campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party said the council includes political leaders, grassroots mobilisers, women and young people from the state’s 13 local government areas and 171 political wards.

According to a statement issued in Abakaliki and signed by state spokesperson Darlington Onwe, the council will coordinate campaign activities across Ebonyi, strengthen voter engagement and mobilise support for the party’s candidates in elective positions. The party said its work would also advance the political ambition of its governorship candidate, Ifeanyi-Chukwuma Odii.

Nwanne Ominyi was named director-general of the campaign, with Paul Okorie appointed deputy director-general for operations. Other named officials include Chigozie Omege, deputy director-general for Ebonyi North; Justus Ikechukwu-Okorie, deputy director-general for Ebonyi South; and Festus Okoha, deputy director-general for Ebonyi Central. Mudi Erenede was appointed director of legal services.

Ikechukwu Nwobo will serve as campaign spokesperson, while Okorie C. Okorie was named director of special duties and protocol. The campaign slogan is “Anyi G’Emeya,” which the statement translates as “Yes, We Can.” The party called on appointees, supporters and stakeholders to show unity, discipline and commitment, and to work together to rebuild and reposition the state.

title: Tinubu urges Igboho to work with security agencies to protect South-West
summary: Tinubu reportedly asked Sunday Igboho’s Iru Ekun network to coordinate with security agencies across the South-West. The appeal followed a rally in Ibadan.
body:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Yoruba activist Sunday Adeyemo, known as Sunday Igboho, to work with government security agencies to improve safety across the South-West, according to a statement from Igboho’s media office. Igboho is the founder of the Iru Ekun Security Network, a home-grown security initiative.

The statement said Tinubu spoke with Igboho inside his official car after an All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan on Saturday. The meeting focused on Iru Ekun’s activities and the need for its operatives to coordinate with the police, Nigerian Army, Department of State Services and other relevant bodies. Igboho’s media office issued the account on Monday in Ibadan, Oyo State.

According to the statement, Tinubu called for Iru Ekun to continue supporting security in rural communities, urban centres and forests across Yorubaland. It said the president highlighted the importance of cooperation in addressing criminality in farming settlements and forest reserves, and of monitoring areas to guard against what the statement described as possible infiltration by terrorists from Lake Chad, Mali and other African countries.

The account also said Iru Ekun was asked to provide security to Nigerians within its areas of operation regardless of ethnicity, religion or political affiliation. It added that the network should inform security agencies before carrying out its security duties, with the aim of improving coordination and public confidence in the government’s responsibility to protect residents. The appeal for cooperation comes ahead of the January 2027 general elections, which the statement cited as a period when efforts to address insecurity in Yoruba states would be important.

title: Kenyan court declines bid to freeze Dangote’s $327 million pipeline stake
summary: Kenya’s High Court declined an immediate freeze on Aliko Dangote’s 24.76% stake in Kenya Pipeline Company. A petition over the share transactions remains pending.
body:
Kenya’s High Court has declined to impose immediate restrictions on dealings in Aliko Dangote’s 24.76% stake in Kenya Pipeline Company, acquired in a transaction valued at approximately $327 million. The court has not yet ruled on the legality of the transaction or the allegations raised in the petition.

Justice Patricia Nyaundi Mande issued directions on November 10, 2026, in a case filed by human rights activist Francis Awino. The petition asks the court to restrict dealings in the shares while it considers whether the public institutions involved properly authorised their acquisition and subsequent disposal. The judge declined to certify the application as urgent or grant orders before hearing from the other parties.

Respondents must file replies by November 27, with the case scheduled for mention on November 30. Those dates fall shortly before Kenya Pipeline Company’s annual general meeting on December 2. Dangote’s investment vehicle is expected to move towards nominating a director ahead of the meeting, potentially replacing the National Social Security Fund’s representative on the board. The court’s decision does not resolve the petition or establish that the transactions complied with applicable requirements.

The dispute concerns how public institutions acquired, held and later disposed of shares in the company following its privatisation. Awino is seeking greater disclosure of transactions involving shares held by public institutions and pension funds, including the National Social Security Fund, Public Service Superannuation Fund, County Pension Fund, Lapfund and Laptrust. The petition also refers to pension schemes linked to Kenya Power, Kenya Pipeline Company and Kenya Ports Authority. The case remains a challenge over disclosure and transaction approvals, not an established finding of wrongdoing.

title: Kwankwaso Asked Me To Swear By Qur’an Over APC Deal With Tinubu, Abba Yusuf Alleges
summary: Abba Yusuf says Rabiu Kwankwaso asked him to promise a return to the APC if courts upheld his 2023 election. Kwankwaso has denied any deal with Tinubu.
body:
Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf says his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, asked him to promise President Bola Tinubu that they would return to the All Progressives Congress (APC) if the legal challenge to Yusuf’s 2023 election victory proceeded without interference. Yusuf made the allegation in an interview with BBC Hausa presenter Aminu Kutama, discussing his January 2026 move from the New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) to the APC.

Yusuf said Kwankwaso sent him to meet Tinubu shortly after the election, which was being challenged by the APC candidate, Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna. He said the instruction was to convey their commitment to reunite with the APC if Yusuf prevailed, adding that Kwankwaso told him to swear by the Qur’an if necessary. Yusuf also said Kwankwaso held meetings with Tinubu and sent delegations to discuss the proposed arrangement.

According to Yusuf, lawmakers and local government chairmen took part in the discussions, which he said were conducted with Kwankwaso’s knowledge. He alleged that the understanding fell apart after Kwankwaso made public remarks opposing the deal, and that those comments were relayed to Tinubu. Yusuf rejected the suggestion that his defection betrayed his former mentor, saying he was carrying out an arrangement initiated by Kwankwaso. He added that they had not stopped communicating entirely and that he had recently sent Kwankwaso greetings.

Kwankwaso has previously denied reaching an agreement with Tinubu over the Supreme Court case, saying the court decided the election dispute on its merits. The Supreme Court upheld Yusuf’s victory in January 2024, overturning earlier judgments in favour of Gawuna. Yusuf formally joined the APC on January 26, 2026, ending his longstanding political association with Kwankwaso, who had played a major role in his emergence as governor. Yusuf’s account offers a different version of the political discussions surrounding the election challenge and the subsequent breakdown in relations.

title: Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS
summary: CAS says it will rule Tuesday on Senegal’s appeal against the decision to award Morocco the Africa Cup of Nations title. The dispute stems from January’s final in Rabat.
body:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) says it will deliver its decision on Tuesday on Senegal’s appeal against the removal of its Africa Cup of Nations title. In a statement issued Monday, the court said the parties had been told the ruling would be released during the afternoon of November 24, 2026, Greenwich Mean Time. CAS did not announce what the outcome would be.

The appeal concerns the final played in Rabat on January 18. Senegal initially won 1-0 against Morocco after Pape Gueye scored in extra time. But the match was disrupted late in normal time, when Senegal players left the pitch to protest a penalty awarded to Morocco while the score was still 0-0.

The players later returned, with the match delayed for almost 20 minutes. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted to enter the pitch. In March, the Confederation of African Football overturned the result, recording a 3-0 victory for Morocco and awarding the country the title.

The Senegalese Football Federation condemned that decision as the “most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport”. Senegal’s team also paraded the trophy before supporters in Paris at the end of March. CAS heard the appeal behind closed doors at its Lausanne headquarters on October 8. Tuesday’s ruling will determine whether CAF’s decision to award Morocco the title stands or is overturned.

title: Gombe awards seven road contracts covering 97km
summary: Gombe State has signed contracts for seven roads spanning about 97 kilometres in four local government areas. The projects are intended to improve rural access and trade.
body:
Gombe State has signed agreements with construction companies for seven road projects covering approximately 97 kilometres across Balanga, Kaltungo, Shongom and Yamaltu-Deba local government areas. The state says the roads are intended to connect rural communities, ease the movement of agricultural produce and improve access to markets and other economic opportunities.

The contracts were signed at a ceremony organised by the Ministry of Works and Infrastructure. Commissioner Shehu Yerima Abdullahi said the projects form part of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s infrastructure programme, which aims to extend development beyond urban centres and support rural communities. He instructed contractors to follow approved engineering specifications, quality standards and contract terms, and said the ministry would monitor work to ensure delivery within agreed timelines.

The projects are the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including a spur to Dalawaja; Phase One of the four-kilometre Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road; and the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak. The package also includes the 15-kilometre Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road, the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road, the 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road and the 1.5-kilometre Kunuwal Road Network.

Permanent Secretary Danladi Adamu described the signing as a step towards implementing and supervising the projects. Representatives of EEC International Limited, SWAS GRADE Limited and DATUM Construction Nigeria Limited said their companies would meet the approved specifications and contractual requirements and complete the work within the agreed periods. The State Executive Council approved the seven projects at its most recent meeting, chaired by Governor Yahaya. Once completed, they are expected to reduce travel difficulties, improve rural-urban connections and support the movement of farm produce to markets.

title: TotalEnergies deepens support for vulnerable Nigerians
summary: TotalEnergies donated N5 million each to two Nigerian charities serving elderly people and women with mental health conditions. The gifts were announced at its 2026 charity golf tournament.
body:
TotalEnergies has donated N5 million each to two organisations caring for vulnerable people in Nigeria. The donations were announced at the company’s 2026 Charity Golf Tournament in Port Harcourt, where Country Chair Matthieu Bouyer said the event was intended to raise funds for the charities and support their work in local communities.

The beneficiaries are the Little Sisters of the Poor Home for the Elderly in Enugu and the Rosaline Home Rehabilitation Centre in Ogale, Eleme, Rivers State. The elderly home provides accommodation, meals, medical attention and daily assistance. Bouyer said it had cared for older people in difficult circumstances for more than five decades, regardless of their background or religion.

The rehabilitation centre, operated by the Daughters of Charity of St. Vincent de Paul, supports women with mental health conditions who have experienced homelessness or abandonment. Bouyer said TotalEnergies would add to the tournament proceeds, and encouraged participants and supporters to contribute towards the organisations’ priorities.

Mary Jacinta, the elderly home’s mother superior, welcomed the donation and appealed for further assistance. Established in 1975, the home cares for more than 46 residents, many of whom have physical disabilities or age-related illnesses and need ongoing help with personal needs. Jacinta said the sisters live alongside residents and provide care around the clock, while the home relies on public charity.

She said the donation would help address urgent needs, including renovations to residents’ rooms and adjustable medical beds. The home also faces unreliable electricity and insufficient water supplies, and hopes to install solar power and build a borehole. Jacinta called on individuals and organisations to help improve residents’ welfare and comfort.

title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
summary: The death toll from a boat capsize in Bayelsa has risen to 29, while more than 50 survivors are receiving hospital treatment. Recovery efforts continue.
body:
The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29. Governor Douye Diri gave the figure during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima, saying more than 50 survivors were receiving treatment in hospitals. The final casualty count remains uncertain as recovery teams continue efforts to retrieve the boat. Diri said some passengers might still be trapped inside it.

The accident occurred on November 20, 2026, near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area. The boat was carrying mourners from Ayama Community to a burial ceremony in Ukubie when it capsized at about 11 a.m., according to the Bayelsa State Police Command.
